FT and IAAFT surrogates for bispectral significance testing

Source: R/bispectral_surrogate.R
bispectral_surrogate.Rd

The bispectral_surrogate function generates null-hypothesis surrogate series. Fourier-transform (FT) phase-randomised surrogates preserve the periodogram exactly (all Fourier amplitudes, including DC and the even-length Nyquist bin) while randomising the phases. Iterative amplitude-adjusted Fourier-transform (IAAFT) surrogates (Schreiber and Schmitz, 1996) preserve the observed marginal distribution exactly and iteratively approach the observed Fourier amplitudes; the iteration stops early when the relative spectral error changes by less than 1e-10. The reported relative spectral error is evaluated only on the independent positive frequencies (DC and the even-length Nyquist bin excluded). Translated from Acycle v3.1 bispectralSurrogate.m (Mingsong Li).

Usage

bispectral_surrogate(
  data = NULL,
  type = "iaaft",
  iaaft_iter = 200,
  n_sim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Series to make surrogates of: a numeric vector, or a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and the proxy in column 2 (only column 2 is used; a one-column matrix uses that column). All values must be finite (no NA). Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

type

Kind of surrogate (character): "iaaft" (iterative amplitude-adjusted Fourier transform; keeps the value distribution exactly and the Fourier amplitudes approximately) or "ft" (Fourier phase randomisation; keeps the Fourier amplitudes exactly; "phase" and "fourier" are accepted as synonyms). Case is ignored. Default="iaaft".

iaaft_iter

Maximum number of IAAFT iterations per surrogate (positive integer); the iteration stops earlier when the relative spectral error no longer changes. Ignored when type="ft". Default=200.

n_sim

Number of surrogate series to generate (positive integer); each one becomes a column of the output matrix surrogates. Default=1.

seed

Seed of the random number generator (integer), so that the surrogates can be reproduced; NULL leaves the current random state unchanged. Default=NULL.

verbose

Show a text progress bar over the surrogates (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list with surrogates (matrix, one surrogate per column), type, iterations (completed IAAFT iterations per surrogate, 1 for FT) and relative_spectral_error (per surrogate).

References

Theiler, J., Eubank, S., Longtin, A., Galdrikian, B., Farmer, J.D., 1992. Testing for nonlinearity in time series: the method of surrogate data. Physica D 58, 77-94.

Schreiber, T., Schmitz, A., 1996. Improved surrogate data for nonlinearity tests. Physical Review Letters 77, 635-638.

Author

Michiel Arts (R translation); original MATLAB code: Mingsong Li (Acycle bispectral module).

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
x <- exp(0.35 * as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.75), n = 512)))
sur <- bispectral_surrogate(data = x, type = "iaaft", n_sim = 5, seed = 3)
# marginal distribution preserved exactly
max(abs(sort(sur$surrogates[, 1]) - sort(x)))
#> [1] 0
sur$relative_spectral_error
#> [1] 0.012638533 0.013390366 0.011535024 0.011472739 0.009397641
# }
